title: Las bolsas
goal: Pay somebody to carry your shopping, agreed first
culture: The cargadores carry loads on their backs and by handcart, and it is a job like any other. Agreeing the price before he picks anything up is the whole etiquette and it protects both of you — afterwards it is an argument, beforehand it is a price.

beats.es: ¿Le ayudo con eso, jefe? Está pesado.
beats.en: Yes, give me a hand, please.
beats.good: Me ayuda asks for a hand rather than hiring a servant, which is how both of you want it framed.
Distance here is corners and blocks. Nobody measures anything in metres and nobody uses a street name.

beats.es: Va pues. Ahorita se lo dejo ahí.
beats.objective: Ask the price before he lifts it
beats.en: And what will you charge me?
beats.good: Before he picks it up, every time. Ask afterwards and you are having an argument; ask now and you are agreeing a price.

beats.es: Deme veinte pesos y estamos bien.
beats.good: Quedamos así seals it: we are agreed. It closes every small deal in this country and it is worth more than a handshake.
